process.title: I use structure before speed.
process.description: My logic background shows up in how I define a product: clarify the premises, map the rules, test the flow, and keep the final output reviewable.

steps.title: Find the real problem
steps.label: PROBLEM
steps.description: Start from a concrete workflow, repeated task, or decision that is difficult to handle today.

steps.title: Map the user flow
steps.label: FLOW
steps.description: Define inputs, system states, review points, outputs, and fallback paths before building UI.

steps.title: Build a clickable version
steps.label: PROTOTYPE
steps.description: Use AI-assisted coding to create a working interface that can be tested, not just described.

steps.title: Test the judgment
steps.label: TEST
steps.description: Use realistic data, mobile interactions, and edge cases to see whether the flow holds up.

steps.title: Turn it into a case
steps.label: DELIVER
steps.description: Package the product, documentation, deployment, and reflection so the work can be evaluated.

about.title1: Logic trains how I structure a problem.
about.title2: Product practice tests it in the interface.
about.bio1: I’m Jamie Zhang, a graduate student in logic at China University of Political Science and Law. My background helps me structure ambiguous problems into assumptions, rules, decisions, and conclusions.
about.bio2: I bring that habit into AI product work: defining the problem, mapping the flow, shaping AI output, building frontend prototypes, writing documentation, and deploying the result independently.
about.opportunity: I’m looking for AI product and LLM application roles where product thinking, structured analysis, and hands-on prototyping matter.
